title: I Used the Community Rain-Barrel Tap Hours on the Chair Who Filled Extra Jugs

parts.text: I opened tap three at 7:04 a.m. and chair Eden was already filling past our numbered allotment. The stencil said: ONE BARREL. TWO JUGS. TAP FOLLOWS THE HOURS. I was forty-six, garden steward, holding a card that listed our plot. Eden shrugged. "Chairs are the rain." I photographed the stencil, the card, and her third jug on our spigot. Then I asked for the tap log. At 7:12 horticulture pinged why Eden's name was on our two. I kept my voice garden-soft and let the timestamp talk. A stencil is only a stencil until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Horticulture can see Eden's third jug on our spigot during our hours.

social.video_title: She filled a third jug on our numbered tap — Part 1/2
social.description: Rain barrel, a chair on our spigot, a two-jug stencil she posted. I logged the third. Would you have asked for the tap log?

parts.text: Eden called it overflow until horticulture asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the stencil, and the jug still. The tap went back to our two. Eden ran her own hours and told the next chair atmosphere was always about drought. Drought is a word chairs use when a stencil exists. Barrel policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE RAIN. I keep our card on a labeled clip. Eden brown-bags her jokes. The garden finally looks like hours, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the rain — Part 2/2
social.description: Tap log, numbered allotment, and a second line on the stencil. Was overflow ever our third jug?
